subject: Critical-path decision log + QBR artifact requests
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Kate Morales <kate@aptlyhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudprime.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Critical-path decision log + QBR artifact requests

Team + Kate —

As we approach the mid-quarter checkpoint and the QBR with Aptly (scheduled 2026-08-05), I want to lock a short decision log and call out the artifacts we need to land by next Thursday (7/29) so the QBR pack is sane. High level: we have three scope decisions that materially affect throughput and cost projections in the QBR (two are internal, one depends on Aptly confirmation).

1) Feature-level rescope: push the realtime prefetch work to Q4 and keep the mid-run cache + batching optimizations for Q3. Impact: reduces infra delta by ~35% on our Q3 estimate but increases short-term latency for certain flows.

2) Evaluation cadence: cut the manual prompt-eval sweep down to top-20 regressions (from 50) for the QBR artifacts; full sweep remains in the backlog for Aug.

3) Aptly decision (external): whether they will accept a 99.5% P99 latency SLA for their production burst window or require 99.9%. That will determine if we configure reserved capacity for their Dedicated pool.

Requests / asks (owners + due dates in parentheses):
- Populate decision log with rationale + cost delta for each decision (Karthik, 7/23)
- Naomi to collate top-20 prompt-eval results and a one-slide summary (Naomi, 7/27)
- Stephanie to prepare the QBR artifact checklist + slides (Stephanie, 7/29)
- Kate / Aptly to confirm SLA target and peak burst profile (Kate, 7/26)

I've attached a working spreadsheet (critical_path_decision_log.xlsx) and a QBR artifact checklist stub to get us started. Please reply with any objections to the three decisions above within 24 hours; otherwise we'll treat them as accepted for QBR planning.

Thanks — short and focused here so we can get to the doc.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Sent from my laptop
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Kate Morales <kate@aptlyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Critical-path decision log + QBR artifact requests

Vanessa —

Thanks, flagged. Two quick points from the CS / Delivery side before we lock: 

- The realtime prefetch push to Q4 is acceptable if we commit a mitigation: increase cache retention for top-10 prefixes and enable cold-start warmup during off-peak batch windows. I can scope that and put the operator runbook in the spreadsheet (Naomi, 7/24).
- For the prompt-eval cut to top-20: agree for QBR as long as we include a short note about selection bias (we'll call it out on the slide). I will also surface the 3 highest-severity regressions with example prompts.

On the Aptly SLA question — Kate, if you could confirm burst window hours and expected concurrent streams, that helps Karthik size capacity and estimate cost.

I'll start populating the spreadsheet with the mitigation plan and sample prompts.

-Naomi
Principal, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Kate Morales <kate@aptlyhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:38:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Critical-path decision log + QBR artifact requests

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clarity. A couple of quick clarifications from Aptly: 

- For the SLA: our internal ops team prefers 99.9% P99 for production during our clinical reporting window (Mon-Fri, 08:00-14:00 ET). We can accept 99.5% for exploratory/dev traffic. If the delta in cost for 99.9% is large, we may opt to reserve critical job types and run everything else on burst.
- Peak concurrency: typical concurrent streams are 18–25 (30 spikes during reporting windows).
- Procurement: we need a simple T&Cs doc and expected invoice cadence for any Dedicated reservation options. I cc'd our procurement alias.

We can confirm formally by 7/26 after we run the team through the projected cost scenarios.

—Kate
Head of Data Ops, Aptly Health
kate@aptlyhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Kate Morales <kate@aptlyhealth.com>, procurement@cloudprime.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Critical-path decision log + QBR artifact requests

Folks —

I've updated the attached spreadsheet with two cost scenarios: 99.5% P99 (reserved capacity not required) and 99.9% P99 (reserved Dedicated pool with minimal burst). Key notes: 

- Delta in monthly infra cost between scenarios: ~42% for our modeled profile (I included conservative network egress in the calc).
- Operational burden: 99.9% requires a small on-call rotation for warmup during reporting windows; we estimate one on-call engineer shared across two accounts.
- Risk: if Aptly confirms 99.9% and we don't reserve, tail spikes could push latency above target during multi-customer events; fallback policy would be to route to a higher-cost variant (we document this as an emergency runbook).

Actionable next steps I propose (and I added them to the sheet):
- Kate: confirm SLA & peak hours (7/26) — once we have this we can lock scenario and invoice cadence language for procurement
- Naomi: one-pager on the top-3 regressions and one-slide summary (7/27)
- Stephanie: finalize QBR skeleton + slide placeholders (7/29)
- Vanessa: assemble decision log into the executive summary for the QBR and route for review (7/29)

I'll keep the sheet live. If no objections by EOD Friday we proceed with the 99.5% plan for QBR prep and present the two scenarios to Aptly during the QBR.

Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
Attachments: critical_path_decision_log.xlsx, qbr_artifact_checklist.pdf
